$comment: Hand-labelled ground truth over real captured records in fixtures/records.json.
Every value here was read off the source record, not guessed. Where a record
genuinely does not state a field, the label is null and an extractor that
invents a value is marked wrong for it.
'representation' is the field the product's conclusions rest on and it is
graded with no partial credit. The cases are chosen to cover all four states,
including the ones that are easy to get wrong: multi-country trials where the
region is one site among fourteen, and reviews that never say who was studied.
'condition_accept' lists surface forms that should count, so an extractor
answering 'type 2 diabetes' is not marked wrong against 'Diabetes Mellitus,
Type 2'. Grading meaning, not string equality.

cases.note: India is one recruiting country out of fourteen. This is the case a naive extractor gets wrong in both directions: 'none' because most sites are elsewhere, or 'primary' because India appears at all.
Nepal and Pakistan among six countries.
Condition is deliberately unlabelled: the record lists fourteen of them and there is no single defensible answer, so scoring it would be scoring a coin toss.
Hong Kong is Asia but not South Asia. A country-list heuristic that matches on 'Asia' fails here.
A narrative review of incretin therapies. No population at all. Must be 'unclear', never 'none'.
The country is never named. It has to be inferred from Medicare and '44 states'. No regex reaches this; it is the clearest single case for the model.
Systematic review of undiagnosed T2DM across South Asia. Primary, even though no single country is the population.
Captured under the diabetes query but is actually about drug allergy. Tests whether the extractor reports the condition the paper studied rather than the one we searched for.
